title: Throughput cliff shepherd and rapid rollout to address tokens/sec + first-token surge
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden throughput cliffs (tokens/sec drop) and elevated first-token times (TTFT) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments after a staggered rollout of scheduler micro-optimizations on 2026-03-09. This ticket coordinates the diagnosis, short-term mitigation (hotpatch), and controlled rollout of a stable fix across environments, plus follow-up observability and postmortem.
observed_behavior: Starting ~2026-03-09 02:00 UTC we saw a 30-60% drop in sustained tokens/sec in multi-tenant clusters and a 2-4x increase in 95th percentile TTFT for affected models. The failures were intermittent and correlated with microburst request patterns (many short prompts) and multi-model serving (model fan-out). Metrics indicated queues growing on the scheduler side and long tail RPC retry counts to GPU workers.
hypothesis_and_root_cause: Preliminary root cause: a configuration drift caused the adaptive scheduling window to revert to a fixed window size during a gradual rollout. The fixed window misaligned batch boundaries under spiky short-request workloads, causing microbatches to be sent with suboptimal packing and creating starvation pockets on a subset of worker shards. On Dedicated and Private clusters, an interaction with per-tenant throttles amplified the effect, turning transient queueing into a sustained throughput cliff. Related: a kernel variant probe that had been enabled in the same rollout sometimes forced slower int8 kernels for short-context paths, compounding tokens/sec loss.
mitigation_steps_taken: 1) Emergency revert of scheduled rollout flag to previous adaptive-window behavior (hosted & dedicated rolled back 02:45 UTC). 2) Deployed a hotpatch that adds a temporary per-deployment override to force adaptive batching for short-request workloads. 3) Injected a soft-throttle gate at ingress for new short-session flows to smooth microburst arrivals. 4) Opened an emergency canary in one EU region for the full fix before global rollout. 5) Notified affected customers and enabled customer-level graceful fallback model variants where available.
timeline: 2026-03-09 01:50 UTC: Pager alert: sustained tokens/sec drop in prod-cluster-04
2026-03-09 02:10 UTC: Triage: correlation with scheduler rollout flag (srv-window-v2) identified
2026-03-09 02:45 UTC: Immediate rollback of srv-window-v2 on Hosted and Dedicated; Private customers notified and given opt-out guidance
2026-03-09 03:30 UTC: Hotpatch deployed to enforce adaptive batching for short requests (hotpatch #GH-4286)
2026-03-09 04:15 UTC: Soft-throttle gate enabled at ingress for new short-session flows
2026-03-09 06:00 UTC: Metrics show partial recovery (tokens/sec +35%, TTFT p95 down 30%) in canary region
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Began controlled canary rollout of full scheduler fix; customer bridge stood up
runbook_steps: Step 1: If tokens/sec drop detected, enable per-deployment override: POST /admin/config?scheduler_window=adaptive
Step 2: If queues on scheduler > 80% for > 2 minutes, enable ingress soft-throttle: POST /admin/traffic_shaper?mode=soft
Step 3: Route affected customers to fallback model variant via routing policy (console -> routes -> add fallback)
Step 4: If RPC retry rate spikes, increase worker-concurrency limit for ephemeral shard (use host-level override)
Step 5: Open customer bridge and run osc-check-list (link in runbook)
postmortem_notes_and_actions: Action A: Harden rollout gating to require synthetic microburst workload test before enabling scheduler changes (owned by infra-team)
Action B: Add surge detector based on short-request burst rate and tokens/sec slope to catch cliffs before customers escalate (owned by telemetry)
Action C: Add end-to-end canary across Hosted/Dedicated/Private within the same rollout plan (owned by release)
Action D: Rework kernel probe to avoid forcing int8 variant for short-context paths without explicit latency budget check (owned by runtime)
Action E: Update runbooks and customer communication templates for cross-deployment escalations
observed_postfix_metrics: After hotpatch and rollback: tokens/sec recovered ~40-80% depending on cluster, TTFT p95 improved by ~25-45% in canary and then global patches. Some private clusters required manual opt-in to rollback by customer infra teams, which prolonged impact windows.

2026-03-09 07:00 UTC: Status update: partial recovery and ongoing controlled rollout

notes_for_qa: Create synthetic microburst workload harness that emits many short (<= 32 token) requests interleaved with long-context requests. Validate tokens/sec stability across scale states and confirm scheduler window adaptation prevents cliff under 500 req/s bursts. Include Dedicated and Private cluster runs.
